title: Mobile App Development in Dallas
metaTitle: Mobile App Development in Dallas, TX | TDM
metaDescription: iOS and Android apps for Dallas startups and established companies: UX research, native or cross-platform builds, and App Store and Google Play release.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) designs and builds iOS and Android apps for Dallas startups and established companies. We build native apps in Swift and Kotlin when performance and platform feel matter most, and cross-platform apps in Flutter or React Native when budget and speed to market come first. We take each app from research and design through to release on the App Store and Google Play. In Dallas the request comes as often from an operations manager with staff in the field as from a founder with a consumer idea.

sections.heading: The apps Dallas businesses actually commission
paragraphs: Dallas is a corporate city, and much of its app demand is practical. A roofing company wants inspectors to photograph damage, measure a roof and send an estimate from the driveway. A logistics firm near the airport wants drivers to confirm deliveries with a signature and a photo. A commercial contractor wants site reports filed from a phone at the end of each day. These apps never appear in a store chart, but they remove hours of paperwork.

Consumer apps here tend to come from restaurants and hospitality groups that want ordering and loyalty in their own hands, from fitness studios and medical or cosmetic practices that want booking and reminders, and from property firms. There is also an active startup scene, partly fed by people leaving large employers in telecoms, finance and semiconductors with a product in mind.

sections.heading: Building for a metro this wide
paragraphs: The Metroplex covers a great deal of ground, and that affects design more than people expect. Field staff spend the day driving between jobs from Fort Worth to McKinney, so their app must be quick to use with one hand in a parked truck and readable in hard summer sunlight. New subdivisions on the northern edge can have weak signal, so forms and photos should save on the device and sync later.

Data rules also need attention early. Apps that hold patient information fall under federal health privacy law, and Texas has its own consumer data privacy law. We design sign-in, storage and permissions with that in mind, and your legal adviser should confirm which obligations apply to you.

sections.heading: How we take an app from idea to store
paragraphs: We begin by defining the one job the app must do well, who will use it and how success will be measured. Then come user flows and screen designs you can click through before any code is written.
bullets: UX research, personas and a scoped first version.
Interface design that follows Apple and Google guidelines, which makes store review smoother.
Native or cross-platform development, chosen for the app and not for our convenience.
A secure back end, an admin panel and connections to your CRM, booking or payment systems.
Testing on real devices, then developer account setup, store listings and review submission.

sections.heading: Before you sign with an app developer
paragraphs: Confirm that the developer accounts with Apple and Google will be registered in your company's name, so the app is yours. Ask whether a mobile-friendly website would do the job for less, which is sometimes true. Request test builds on your own phone during development, and do not accept screenshots in their place.

presence: TDM is not based in Dallas. We work with Dallas companies remotely: workshops and design reviews take place on video calls, and test builds are sent to your own devices so you can try each version as it is completed.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to build an app in Dallas?
faqs.a: That depends on scope: the number of screens and features, whether it needs a back end and integrations, and whether you want native or cross-platform. A quote follows a free consultation.

faqs.q: Should we build native or cross-platform?
faqs.a: Cross-platform frameworks such as Flutter and React Native suit most business apps and cover iOS and Android from one codebase. Native development is the better choice when the app leans heavily on device hardware or needs the highest performance. We recommend one after discovery.

faqs.q: Do you handle App Store and Google Play submission?
faqs.a: Yes. We set up the developer accounts in your name, prepare listings, screenshots and metadata, submit for review and deal with any questions from Apple or Google.

faqs.q: How long does app development take?
faqs.a: That depends on what the app has to do. A scoped first version is quicker than a full product, and the schedule is set out in the plan once discovery is complete.
